claim: The design record quotes a plain two-level hierarchy, 'no inner level is ever needed for 7-10 fields', while the protocol says the tree has three levels, never more.
The design takes a leaf fill factor of 0.75 from the B+ tree, but no script reads fill_factor and tcb/plan-tree.mjs does not exist, so the packing at 0.75 appears only in the cost prototype.
The design record moves to later a plan-tree bulk load, redistribution and a split with a separator.
Sibling links and copy-on-write are the two extra options (+2) under D2-02, not the selected design, and the same row keeps sibling links as a one-line pointer only.
An attack round judged that the tree as a plain hierarchy earns its place and the B+ tree analogy does not.
The protocol's level 0 is the coordinator, level 1 is one pack builder and then one expert per field, and level 2 is helpers (readers Sonnet, checkers Opus) that never start other agents.
Experts never see each other's output, and everything passes through files that the coordinator checks (protocol v1).

The design record gives pack capacity as 300,000 - 60,000 - 60,000 = 180.0k tokens, while the code computes W_quality - child_prefix_tokens - review_reserve_tokens, which is 165,000 tokens with the review reserve at 75k (research-tree/tcb/commit.mjs:760-763).
The design record lists as later the plan-tree bulk load, the hook budget check, redistribution and split with a separator, and tcb/plan-tree.mjs does not exist.

The library does not hold a record of the owner rejecting removal of the split (lookup on split, B+ tree, hierarchy and shape found none), and the protocol withdraws 'Split a field in two on overflow'.
Protocol v2 R50 states the hand-over law of Harris 1913 and Young 1974: tokens per work call are least at k* = sqrt(2H0/g), so W* = P + S + sqrt(2H0 x g).

The 2026-11-16 design step, run as a Workflow rather than a session tree, used 1,484,854 tokens for the map (16 agents, 12 minutes) and 2,743,461 tokens for the design, model and attack (15 agents, 82 minutes).
admit.mjs decide(facts) is a pure function that gives reasons for a refusal by slots, memory and budget, and its budget term applies only when B_tokens is set, which is null today.

None of the 13 fixes in research-tree/BUILD-SIZE.md touches the tree's shape, capacity, split or overflow, and a change of shape would touch admit.mjs, replace.mjs, status.mjs and watch.mjs, the files ten fixes already edit.

Record b1-0121 says the tree's run-time writers share no work file: a child writes only its own staging folder, objects are stored by exclusive create and never repaired, and two disagreeing verdicts make the item 'unclear'.
Starting a session goes through replace.mjs start, which runs admit decide inside the run lock, and a fixed prefix of about 60,000 tokens is spent per agent before any work.
There is no router for search: question keys are approved question ids with one owning field (protocol v2 R46), and no token or time cost of a routing step is recorded.
A new field needs an amendment (protocol v1, line 278).

A split that hands half a range to a new session is not built (design R48(d)), and the research the old leaf already paid for cannot be divided: 'a B+ split costs one node copy; here the data is paid for and the window cannot be divided'.
There is no merge; the protocol says 'Height, search, latches and merges add nothing'.
Rebalance is not built: redistribution to a sibling is later (R48(c)), and the design text says to redistribute an overflow range to a sibling with slack, else defer.
The coordinator epoch ce and the handover.mjs init, raise and bind commands are built.
H_max = 2 hand-overs plus parks per task is marked 'guess' in research-tree/tcb/thresholds.json:11.
There is no buffer: a child's 400-character note per commit goes straight to the coordinator.
A helper (reader or checker) is a third level that starts no agent, and its result is returned as cards that the child writes.
